sentences.text: Cuspirostrisornis is an extinct genus of bird belonging to the subclass Enantiornithes.
The only known species, Cuspirostrisornis houi, is classified within the family Avisauridae.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — represents a small perching bird with a skull measuring about 27 millimeters in length.
Its skull possessed ten pairs of tiny teeth, five located in the premaxilla and five in the anterior dentary.
The describer Hou noted that the pointed snout was proportionally similar to the beaks of modern wagtails.
The ulna is large and derived, featuring an S-shape similar to that of modern flying birds.
The sternum is described as large, carinate, and broad.
The animal is known from a single fossil found in the Jiufotang Formation in Liaoning province, China.
The holotype fossil was collected in 1993 by Dr. Hou Lianhai and Hou Jinfeng.
The holotype fossil is cataloged as IVPP V 10897.
The generic name derives from Latin words meaning "pointed" and "beak".
The specific name refers to the describer, Mr. Hou Jinfeng.
The genus Cuspirostrisornis was described by Hou in 1997.
The genus Cuspirostrisornis is part of the parent group Cuspirostrisornithidae.
Cuspirostrisornis lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically the Aptian age, approximately 120.3 million years ago.
It is debated whether tooth-bearing prehistoric birds like Cuspirostrisornis possessed a horny beak over their toothed snouts.
While only one species is known, some researchers believe Cuspirostrisornis houi is a synonym of the similar species Cathayornis yandica.
